name: System Owner/User Discovery
description: Adversaries may attempt to identify the primary user, currently logged in user, set of users that commonly uses a system, or whether a user is actively using the system. They may do this, for example, by retrieving account usernames or by using [OS Credential Dumping](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003). The information may be collected in a number of different ways using other Discovery techniques, because user and username details are prevalent throughout a system and include running process ownership, file/directory ownership, session information, and system logs. Adversaries may use the information from [System Owner/User Discovery](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1033) during automated discovery to shape follow-on behaviors, including whether or not the adversary fully infects the target and/or attempts specific actions. Various utilities and commands may acquire this information, including whoami. In macOS and Linux, the currently logged in user can be identified with w and who. On macOS the dscl . list /Users | grep -v '_' command can also be used to enumerate user accounts. Environment variables, such as %USERNAME% and $USER, may also be used to access this information. On network devices, [Network Device CLI](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/008) commands such as `show users` and `show ssh` can be used to display users currently logged into the device.(Citation: show_ssh_users_cmd_cisco)(Citation: US-CERT TA18-106A Network Infrastructure Devices 2018)

telemetry.name: Command Execution
telemetry.description: Execution of a command and its interpreter or parent context.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect process command lines and relevant shell/interpreter audit; shell history alone is neither complete nor tamper-resistant.

providers.name: PowerShell Script Block Logging
providers.scope: Script content via event 4104 when configured; channel depends on PowerShell edition.

providers.name: Sysmon process events
providers.scope: Interpreter launch and parent context, not full script content.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: execve-family execution context; shell built-ins need additional instrumentation.

configuration: Enable Script Block Logging through the policy/configuration for the installed edition. Forward Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational for Windows PowerShell, or PowerShellCore/Operational for PowerShell 7.
Retain script-block ID and fragment ordering alongside process creation. Protect access to collected script text; secrets may be included.
On Linux, use narrowly scoped Audit execution rules for the lab account and supported architectures, and retain joined SYSCALL/EXECVE/PATH records.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Script content and process command lines are different signals. Logging may be partial, fragmented, filtered or disabled; never assume a command line reveals everything executed.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per host role and principal: rare interpreters, command argument patterns and parent-child sequences. Normalize scripts carefully; obfuscation, administrative automation and missing command lines change visibility.

telemetry.name: OS API Execution
telemetry.description: Instrumented operating-system API calls and their return values.
telemetry.collection_focus: Use an approved EDR trace or instrument the owned lab process at selected APIs. Define API name, caller, sanitized arguments and return status.

providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

telemetry.description: Creation of a process with executable, command line, parent and security context.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect Sysmon ProcessCreate (1); preserve ProcessGuid and parent identifiers. Security 4688 is an alternative with separate audit/command-line settings.

strategies.name: Behavioral Detection of User Discovery via Local and Remote Enumeration

analytics.name: Analytic 0254
analytics.guidance: Adversary launches built-in system tools (e.g., whoami, query user, net user) or scripts that enumerate user account information via local execution or remote API queries (e.g., WMI, PowerShell).

tuning.description: Identify if enumeration originates from non-interactive shell or system service
Tune temporal grouping of enumeration + lateral movement attempts
Flag unexpected users issuing enumeration commands (e.g., service accounts)

analytics.name: Analytic 0255
analytics.guidance: Adversary runs commands like `whoami`, `id`, `w`, or `cat /etc/passwd` from non-interactive or scripting contexts to enumerate system user details.

tuning.description: Tune detection based on argument presence (e.g., `cat /etc/passwd` vs. `cat` alone)
Identify if command issued via cron, systemd, or reverse shell
Define how often user/account commands are expected on endpoint

analytics.name: Analytic 0256
analytics.guidance: Adversary uses `dscl`, `who`, or environment variables like `$USER` to identify accounts or sessions via Terminal or malicious LaunchAgents.

tuning.description: Correlate dscl usage with known persistence vectors
Distinguish between user-initiated terminal vs. script execution
Regex-based pattern tuning for `dscl . -list /Users` + grep filters

analytics.name: Analytic 0257
analytics.guidance: Adversary executes CLI commands like `show users`, `show ssh`, or attempts to dump AAA user lists from routers or switches.

tuning.description: Expected command set per device role/user role combination
Correlate access with core vs. edge vs. management plane sensitivity
Detect burst usage of `show` or `debug` commands by non-admin users

candidates.description: Use the PowerShell "GetCurrent" method of the WindowsIdentity .NET class to identify the logged user.

candidates.description: Find existing user session on other computers. Upon execution, information about any sessions discovered will be displayed.

candidates.name: System Owner/User Discovery
candidates.description:
Identify System owner or users on an endpoint

Upon successful execution, sh will stdout list of usernames.

candidates.name: System Discovery - SocGholish whoami
candidates.description:
SocGholish performs whoami discovery commands and outputs the results to a tmp file. 
The test will generate a filename similar to the random one generated during execution and write the file to AppData\Temp.

Reference: https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/threats/socgholish/

candidates.name: System Owner/User Discovery
candidates.description:
Identify System owner or users on an endpoint.

Upon successful execution, cmd.exe will spawn multiple commands against a target host to identify usernames. Output will be via stdout. 
Additionally, two files will be written to disk - computers.txt and usernames.txt.

candidates.name: User Discovery - whoami
candidates.description:
Identify the current user account and security context using whoami. Adversaries use this command during initial
reconnaissance after gaining access to a system to determine the user and privilege level they are operating under.

candidates.name: System Owner/User Discovery Using Command Prompt
candidates.description: Identify the system owner or current user using native Windows command prompt utilities.

candidates.name: User Discovery With Env Vars PowerShell Script
candidates.description: Use the PowerShell environment variables to identify the current logged user.
